# Contextual compile-time parameter headers

This informed [Issue #33](https://github.com/MGYamada/Qleisli/issues/33) study
retains eight first desired/control projects and actual observations in
[the session](session.json). It is not a blind model benchmark.

Attempt-01 has an observer-authored manifest mistake (`schema`); all sixteen
first observations rejected the project before parsing. Attempt-02 changes
only that key to `schema-version`; every QLI byte is unchanged. Its sixteen
baseline observations reach actual const parser refusals, while ordinary
const-name controls pass and the old static header retains its selected/project
profile distinction. Initial observations remain fixed.

The after records use identical repaired programs with contextual const header
support. Nat, Basis and operation selected entries pass. Duplicate and unused
invalid definitions reject; missing markers teach const. Ordinary const-named
functions and the temporary static header keep their outcome. Four zero/three
Nat checks compare canonical and legacy paths with unchanged types/bindings.

The separately saved post-implementation closed client first used the wrong
bare Bit specialization and then a private selected entry. Both actual
refusals and all three source versions remain. The explicit type(Bit) and
public-entry repairs check and return the independently expected classical
zero. These clients are not labelled pre-implementation first attempts.

These are bounded checks and runtime observations, not general source
preservation or constitutional discharge. No checker rule, provider capability,
capacity, edition or dependency is changed. The old header is temporary input:
active-client migration and retirement remain required #33 work.
